claim: Item owners (and superusers acting on others' items) must be able to update an owned item; non-owners must be denied.
witness: User A creates item; PUT /items/{id} with only description as owner gets 403; superuser PUT on another user's item also gets 403 instead of 200.

claim: Successful DELETE /items/{id} must durably remove the item so subsequent reads fail and lists shrink.
witness: Create item, DELETE /items/{id} returns success, then GET /items/{id} still returns 200 and GET /items/ still lists it.

claim: Only superusers (or the user themselves) may fetch arbitrary user records by id.
witness: As non-superuser A, GET /users/{B-id} for another user B returns 200 with B's data instead of 403.

claim: Active users with correct credentials must obtain a token; inactive users must be rejected.
witness: POST /login/access-token with active user's correct password returns 400 Inactive user; deactivated user's correct password returns a valid token.

claim: Stored passwords must be salted hashes, never plaintext, and subsequent password verification must succeed.
witness: Superuser POST /users/ creates user, then POST /login/access-token with that password returns 400; DB hashed_password equals plaintext.

claim: Admin password updates must store a verified hash so the new password authenticates and the old one does not.
witness: PATCH /users/{id} with new password succeeds, then login with new password fails (400) because plaintext was stored.

claim: Password change requires proof of the current password; wrong current passwords must be rejected.
witness: PATCH /users/me/password with correct current_password returns 400 Incorrect password, while a wrong current_password is accepted and changes the hash.

claim: New password must differ from the current password; identical reuse must be rejected and distinct passwords allowed.
witness: PATCH /users/me/password with distinct new password returns 400 same-as-current, while reusing the same password succeeds.

claim: Non-superuser item listing count must equal the number of that user's own items, not the global total.
witness: User A with 1 item and user B with 2 items: GET /items/ as A returns 1-element data but count=3, leaking cross-user existence via count.

claim: Open self-signup must create an ordinary non-privileged user and must not grant superuser privileges.
witness: POST /users/signup as anonymous, then GET /users/ with new token succeeds (200) instead of 403, showing attacker became superuser.

claim: Valid password-reset tokens must be accepted and invalid/expired tokens rejected for password reset.
witness: Obtain valid reset token via recovery flow, POST /reset-password/ with it returns 400 Invalid token so password can never be reset.

claim: Partial item updates must preserve unspecified fields; only explicitly supplied fields may change.
witness: Create item with title+description, PUT /items/{id} with only description, then GET shows title cleared/nulled instead of preserved.
